free_text: The 64-year-old male has an elevated PSA of 6.5 ng/mL and a PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone/apex, with a prior Gleason 3+3 diagnosis. The clinical stage is cT1c. Given the clinical context and imaging findings, active surveillance is recommended pending clinical review of individual treatment benefit and patient preferences. The trade-off involves balancing the risk of progression against the potential morbidity associated with intervention.
